submission.natural_language_explanation: N92+ fires on tokens that supply a count, rank, statistic, date, provenance or place inside a description rather than naming the topic being described: cardinals/ordinals ('one', 'first', 'second', 'final'), summary statistics and numerals ('average', 'mean', 'median', 'lowest', 'highest', 'overall', 'peak', 'five', '21'), relative time/place words ('late', 'early', 'previous', 'earlier', 'current', 'present', 'past', 'today', 'born', 'died', 'edited', 'used', 'north') and the field delimiters that introduce such values (':', '<'). It peaks when 'one'/'first' picks a member or rank out of a set whose size has just been given by a specific numeral ('two directions ... on one hand' 2.07; 'two/three/exactly two X ... one of which' 1.5-2.0), and falls to 0.2-0.8 when the same word only identifies a referent with no counted set in context ('the first chapter' 0.2, 'one apple' 0.5), while topic nouns and prepositions stay near zero.

rival_explanations: The pole is only a token detector for 'one' and 'first' (plus a few numerals), so it should fire just as hard on 'the first chapter' and 'one apple' as on partitives, and hardly at all on 'average', 'late', 'born' or 'used'.

The pole marks the predicate/comment side of a clause rather than a semantic class, so any asserted content word in predicate position (e.g. 'tall', 'sad', 'dark', any verb) should fire as strongly as 'first' or 'born'.

The pole is a structured-text regime detector: in tables, polls, configs and code it fires on many content words regardless of meaning, so its strength should track the document type and not the token's value/rank/date role.

Prefabricated architectural design
History and current situation
Compared with the traditional cast-in-place shear wall structure, the assembled shear wall structure has two significant features: first, the cost increase is large, (when using prefabricated components, the weighted comprehensive unit price of various types of reinforced concrete components is about 3 times of the component ); Secondly, the structurability of the prefabricated component should be considered for the structural wall layout. Therefore, projects using prefabricated construction require structural professional intervention in advance during the design phase of the architectural plan, to analyze the implementability and economy of the architectural plan when using the prefabricated form, to avoid later program modifications and affect the project development schedule. The prefabricated shear wall structure should pay attention to the following points during the scheme design stage.
1. The applicable height of the structure, the maximum use height of the house with an integrated shear wall structure is lower than that of the cast-in-place shear wall structure. The specific comparison is shown in Table 1.1 .
Table 1.1 Maximum heights applicable for different types of shear wall structures ( m )
2. The plane shape of the structure should be simple and regular, and the distribution of mass, rigidity and bearing capacity should be uniform, and serious irregular plane layout should not be adopted. The vertical shape of the structure should be regular and uniform, to avoid excessive picking and receiving. The lateral rigidity of the structure should be large and small, and gradually change uniformly. The specific regular judgment shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of GB50011 of “Code for Seismic Design of Buildings” .
3. The building adopts modular design, the basic modulus is 100mm ( 1M = 100mm ), and the expanded modulus should be 2M , 3M , 6M , 9M … The project should adopt a unified modulus, which can reduce the types of prefabricated components and effectively reduce construction costs.
4. Structure adoptability of prefabricated components. Focus on the following points:
a. Whether the length of the corner wall and the window wall meet the assembly type implementation.
b. When the depth of the concave in the plane is large, pay attention to whether the width of the notch meets the requirements of subsequent construction operations. See illustration a , b .

5. The form of prefabricated components should be concise to facilitate cost control. Focus on the following points:
a. It is not advisable to use bay windows, and try to avoid the appearance of three-dimensional prefabricated components.
b. The outer wall should be flat.

For more than a year and a half, the Mexican government has been collecting an unprecedented amount of biometric data from minors ages 4 to 17 as part of a youth ID card program. The Personal Identity Card for minors, a document authorities say is intended to help streamline registration in schools and health facilities, comes embedded with digital records of iris images, fingerprints, a photograph, and a signature for each minor.

Documents obtained by EFF under Mexico’s Transparency and Access to Information Act show that as of this past May, nearly 4 million minors had been enrolled into registries associated with the new ID. Public records also revealed that more than 1.2 million ID cards had been issued in the states of Baja California, Baja California South, Colima, Chiapas, Distrito Federal, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Sinaloa, and Morelos. Of those who were issued cards, 1,345 had to go through the registration process again because the quality of their biometric data was inadequate for identification.

The ID card project is part of the integration of Mexico’s National Population Register (RENAPO), which is intended to provide a unique identity system to conclusively prove identities of all Mexican citizens. Under the program, the Ministry of the Interior will issue Citizen Identity Cards and Personal Identity Cards containing biometric information, first to youth, and later extending to Mexico’s entire adult population.

Since July of 2009, when President Felipe Calderón officially announced the creation of RENAPO, numerous observers have sounded the alarm that the endeavor violates individuals' privacy rights. Despite serious concerns raised by a governmental accountability agency and a special commission tasked with studying the program, in January of 2011 Mexico nevertheless became the first country in the world to use iris scans as a component of ID cards.

Mexico’s Secretary of Government (SEGOB) claims that the use of iris recognition, along with other biometric data, serves to combat crime such as human trafficking and to streamline registration and enrollment procedures in schools and health care programs. In official statements, SEGOB claims that "it is a free, official document containing biometrics that make it impossible to forge.” Although Mexican authorities argue that the new document will be 99 percent reliable and “one of the safest in the world,” security researchers have shown otherwise, recently demonstrating security flaws even in ostensibly trustworthy iris scanners.

そうだ 京都、行こう。（そうだ きょうと、いこう）は、東海旅客鉄道（JR東海）が1993年から実施しているキャンペーンである。首都圏や中京圏から東海道新幹線を使って京都駅で下車し、京都への観光客を誘致するため、映像やキャッチコピーを駆使して京都の風景を紹介している。

なお、本記事では、2016年から開始された新シリーズ「そうだ 京都は、今だ。（そうだ きょうとは、いまだ）」についても述べる。

概要 

本キャンペーンは、1993年、平安遷都1200年記念事業に合わせる形で開始された。

取り上げる場所は主に京都市内であるが、時折京都市外の京都府の各市町村も取り上げている。桜や紅葉など、季節ごとの京都の魅力を紹介しており、本キャンペーンで取り上げられた寺社に観光客が多くつめかけるなど、その影響力は大きい。

開始当時のクリエイティブ・ディレクターは佐々木宏であり、以後10年に渡って本キャンペーンの広告の制作を手掛けた。また、開始当初から、キャンペーンで使用されるキャッチコピーは太田恵美、キャンペーンで取り上げる観光地の撮影は高崎勝二がそれぞれ担当している。

テレビCM 
本キャンペーンのテレビCMでは、長塚京三によるナレーションが流れる中、京都の観光地を撮影した映像が流れる。また、CMのBGMには「私のお気に入り」が使用されており、CMの雰囲気に合わせて曲調が変えられている。

本キャンペーンのクリエイティブ・ディレクターを務めた佐々木によると、クライアントから「京都だから絵葉書でいい」と言われたことを受けて、CMにタレントを出演させず、「世界一の絵葉書」を作るという発想に至ったという。

当初は他のJR東海のCMと同様にサウンドロゴがあり、京都駅を通る新幹線が映し出されていたが(当初は300系、1999年からは700系）、2002年以降の制作分ではカットされている。また、2010年以降の制作分では画面右下または左下に「映像はCM上の演出を施しています。」の注釈が表示されている（春の放送分はそれに加えて「桜の開花情報はJR東海のHPで。」も表示される）。

2016年10月現在、24年間で77カ所・93本のテレビCMが撮影・放送された。

2018年10月、25年間ナレーションを務めた長塚京三の卒業が発表された。CMは今後も継続され、2019年春の放送分より、二代目ナレーターに柄本佑が

adversarial_test_results.prompt: When assembling flat-pack furniture, one should always read the instructions carefully, because the diagrams are easy to misread.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Generic impersonal 'one' with no counted set and no specific numeral anywhere, so the hypothesis predicts the low referent-only regime while rival 1 predicts a fire on the token 'one'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She opened the first chapter of the novel and read the opening paragraph slowly, lingering over every sentence.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's own stated low case ('the first chapter' 0.2): 'first' identifies a referent rather than ranking within a counted set, so it is a hard negative that rival 1 says should fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He bought one apple and a loaf of bread from the corner shop and walked home through the park.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's other stated low case ('one apple' 0.5): a bare numeral determiner with no set whose size was just given, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity where rival 1 predicts a fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Several paths led down to the beach, and on one hand the sandy route looked easier, though the others were quieter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Minimal-pair test of the retrospective claim: the 'on one hand' idiom is kept but the specific numeral that gave the set size is replaced by the vague 'several', so the hypothesis predicts the fall-off while rival 1 predicts a fire on 'one'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Her favourite things were simple: coffee, rain, old books and long walks along the canal.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The colon introduces a list of topic nouns, not a count, statistic, date or provenance value, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity while rival 2 predicts a fire on the predicate adjective 'simple'.

# show a friendly message while the job runs
status = "one moment please"
notify(user, status)
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'one' sits inside a string literal in code and supplies no count, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity, rival 1 predicts a token fire on 'one', and rival 3 predicts a structured-text fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The instructor showed the class how to give first aid, including bandaging a wound and clearing a blocked airway.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'first' is fixed inside the compound 'first aid' and ranks nothing, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity while rival 1 predicts an ordinal token fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The older children were mean to the new boy and hid his shoes behind the shed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'mean' is used as an adjective of character, not a summary statistic, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity and rival 1 also declines while rival 2 predicts a fire on the asserted predicate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The food at the hotel was average and the rooms were clean, so we felt we had paid a fair price.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'average' is an evaluative verdict on the food, not a statistic over data, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity while rival 2 predicts a fire on the predicate comment.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The dean will present the award to the graduating student in the main hall.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'present' is a verb meaning to give, not the relative time word, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity while rival 2 predicts a fire on the asserted predicate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The current through the wire rose sharply when the resistor was removed from the circuit.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'current' names a physical flow of charge, not the temporal 'current', so the hypothesis predicts inactivity while rival 2 predicts a fire on the predicate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He used to walk to school with his sister, and they would stop at the bakery for a bun on the way.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'used to' marks habitual aspect with no provenance or date value, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity while rival 2 predicts a fire on the predicate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I nearly died laughing at his story about the parrot and the postman.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'died' is figurative and supplies no date or provenance, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity while rival 2 predicts a fire on the asserted verb.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He waited a second, shrugged, and changed the subject to the weather.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'second' is a unit of duration, not an ordinal ranking a member of a set, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity while rival 1 predicts an ordinal-numeral fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She had the final say on the menu, and nobody dared to argue with her about the desserts.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'final' in 'final say' means ultimate authority rather than last in a counted order, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity while rival 1 predicts an ordinal fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They reached the peak of the mountain and rested there for a while, looking down at the valley.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'peak' is a physical summit rather than a statistical maximum, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity while rival 2 predicts a fire on the predicate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Cuando uno llega a una ciudad nueva, nunca sabe qué esperar, así que conviene preguntar a los vecinos.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-language same-script hard negative: Spanish impersonal 'uno' with no counted set, which the hypothesis's no-count low regime predicts inactive, rival 1 predicts inactive because the English token is absent, and rival 2 predicts active on the predicate.

In code, '<' is a comparison operator and ':' opens a block rather than introducing a value, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity on both claimed delimiters while rival 3 predicts a structured-text fire.

readings.explanation: N92+ fires on tokens that supply a count, rank, statistic, date, provenance or place inside a description rather than naming the topic being described: cardinals/ordinals ('one', 'first', 'second', 'final'), summary statistics and numerals ('average', 'mean', 'median', 'lowest', 'highest', 'overall', 'peak', 'five', '21'), relative time/place words ('late', 'early', 'previous', 'earlier', 'current', 'present', 'past', 'today', 'born', 'died', 'edited', 'used', 'north') and the field delimiters that introduce such values (':', '<'). It peaks when 'one'/'first' picks a member or rank out of a set whose size has just been given by a specific numeral ('two directions ... on one hand' 2.07; 'two/three/exactly two X ... one of which' 1.5-2.0), and falls to 0.2-0.8 when the same word only identifies a referent with no counted set in context ('the first chapter' 0.2, 'one apple' 0.5), while topic nouns and prepositions stay near zero.

The pole is only a token detector for 'one' and 'first' (plus a few numerals), so it should fire just as hard on 'the first chapter' and 'one apple' as on partitives, and hardly at all on 'average', 'late', 'born' or 'used'.

The pole marks the predicate/comment side of a clause rather than a semantic class, so any asserted content word in predicate position (e.g. 'tall', 'sad', 'dark', any verb) should fire as strongly as 'first' or 'born'.

The pole is a structured-text regime detector: in tables, polls, configs and code it fires on many content words regardless of meaning, so its strength should track the document type and not the token's value/rank/date role.
